title: the birth of otherworldly: 10 years of integrating art & business
content:
otherworldly is a new creative business born from a decade of integration work as an artist-entrepreneur, and philosophies of world-building.

visit otherworldly

on valentine’s day, I finally released a creative/business/web project that had been actively bubbling in the back of my mind for several months, and simmering in the backrooms of my psyche for a decade — a web alchemy studio called otherworldly.

I built version 1.0 of the website as a container to integrate my philosophies on digital ecosystems & world-building, art & business. it’s both a deeply personal labor of love and collaborative — I’ll be working with my partner Kağan and other developers for custom-build web projects.

I’m calling it a “web alchemy studio” — because the work is about transformation, manifestation, and rebirth — turning brochure websites and brands into living spaces — tender enough to hold the intimacy of solitude, and compelling enough to magnetize a community.

a decade of integrating art + business

I consider myself an artist, writer, and thinker before all else.

I’ve been doing web design work for private clients for almost 10 years, since 2015 — despite never having much of a “sales” page. my clients tend to find me through referrals and word of mouth. I started teaching my approach to web design in 2021, in my first iteration of house on the webs. even then, I knew that I didn’t want to open a typical “design studio” — despite that being the strategic thing to do.

over many years of rejecting traditional marketing advice and social media, I went on a spiraling journey from “artist doing web design services on the side to support herself” — to “artist integrating web design and business — as a manifestation of her creative practice.”

my own journey as an artist-entrepeneur has been slowly learning to see my creativity as my greatest business resource: both for myself, my clients, and anyone who learns from my work.

otherworldly is dedicated channel for sharing those resources.

on multiplicity: three interweaving practices

otherworldly is the integration of 3 practices — each of which is its own channel of resources — services, inspiration, and process/methodology. each of these are ways for visitors and collaborators to engage with otherworldly.

otherworldly is:

  1. a business — a creative services studio for selected clients, offering web design, branding, and illustration/animation.

  2. a creative practice — a creative web experimentation practice for myself & my developers; an artistic playground where the internet is the medium

  3. visionary/guide library — a digital commonwealth of resources, teachings, and courses for values-aligned creatives and entrepreneurs

this model parallels the way in which I approach my work and my ecosystem as a whole — as artist, guide, and entrepreneur. I think about the three of pentacles — the inner collaboration between the spiritual, intellectual, and material selves.

as a working artist, my work has never been one thing — no matter how much I’ve envied people who go to MFAs and can focus on writing a book for two years. I wanted financial autonomy and institutional-independence, which meant I needed to figure out how to have a business. I want my work to engage with the world in a deeper, individual way — by creating new worlds where artistic autonomy and financial agency felt possible, and where creativity is my superpower, not my limitation.

I want otherworldly to have these threads of multiplicity — because more than anything, I want otherworldly to be an expression of a vision — for the liberating creative, connective power that the internet could be in sustaining both our creative and material lives.

birthing & finding business clarity

I mark the birth of otherworldly as the day when I completed the website and made it public — February 14, 2025, at 10:13pm, Istanbul time. otherworldly is an aquarius sun, libra rising, and virgo moon. that is: a nonconformist soul with a keen taste for beauty, and an obsession with the details. a visionary hermit. it’s a 2/5 manifestor with emotional authority, and a right angle cross of contagion 30/29. (the way this parallels my personal human design shocks me…)

I built this first version 1.0 on squarespace, in five sittings, over a month — divided between web design, animations, and writing. within a year, I’m planning for us to migrate to a custom-coded site I’ll design from scratch, developed by my team. this first iteration was about simply creating the vessel.

the hardest part about building otherworldly was not the design or animations — those things feel more like muscle memory and imaginative free-flow. the hardest part, by far, was thinking through and writing out the services page — a business exercise in finding clarity around my pricing and offerings. I went from zero/minimum sales page and word-of-mouth clientele — to these clearly defined business containers.

pricing & boundaries

thinking through pricing has been a deep process around articulating boundaries — structures which will allow me to channel my creative energy — in order to be in my highest service.

otherworldly’s web design and branding intensives take around 4-6 weeks, and start around $7.5k for no or low-code websites, $7k for branding intensives, and $2-3.5k for visual work. custom builds and development would require bigger budgets and far longer timelines, usually a minimum of $20k+.

these rates are still lower than that of design/branding agencies, or boutique graphic design studios — but at the same time, I also know that they’re inaccessible for many in my existing audience of small businesses, service providers, and independent creatives — as well as some of my previous clients. it took me time to clarify and set these new boundaries, and to trust in them.

over the last years, I’ve realized that I’m not the best fit for people who just “need a new website” and don’t feel up to building one — with a squarespace template — themselves. instead, where I thrive is in the work of radical reinvention. I want to push the boundaries in what a website can be — and do — for my clients’ business ecosystems. I want to offer an undiluted, full-power dosing of my creative resources to help them with their transformation.

otherworldly is very much anti-brochure and anti-template, without being inaccessible or haughty. its ethos is about birth, death, and metamorphosis. therefore, what I offer my clients is not just a website execution — but a creative, strategic partnership committed to their business growth. this commitment to process always yields a far better result. to do this, my rates mean that my clients would have to be serious, resourced, and aligned with this philosophy — to want to work together.

as a result, this pricing also means that I can give more of my time and energy to teaching — as well as creating free resources for otherworldly’s archives. my intention is for these archives, to serve, over time, as a digital commonwealth for how and why we build on the internet — with uninhibited imagination, and as channels for creative agency and abundance, in all its forms.

dreams, plans, and expansions

a website is like a book — in that it represents the deep work of integration — work that might have taken months, or years.

otherworldly is my new container to hold creative work, visionary/guide work, and business work. this work has felt too big for keningzhu.com to hold for some time now — and I’m relieved to have finally given it its own home. in looking forward, here’s what I’m imagining…

next few weeks — beginning the otherworldly archives

starting next week, I’ll start writing for otherworldly’s archives — around digital ecosystems, branding & identity work, growing internet businesses, and imaginative web design.

next few months — creating new website experiments

this year, I’m learning how to code — and I’ll start by designing small, experimental websites for my artistic projects under otherworldly studios.


next year — products, apps, & games

for now, otherworldly only offers client services in website design, branding, and illustration/animation. but I’ve talked with Kağan about expanding our work to building games, apps, creative widgets, and more interactive experiences. this makes both of us super, super excited.

*

as I’m moving my writings around digital ecosystems more towards otherworldly, in the meantime, kening zhu — this place, as my artist home — will be focused more deeply on creative process, artist-business philosophies, intuitive guidance, curated inspiration, and my vision for what art can be — as a creative, generative resource for life. thank you for being on this journey with me.
